chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Musa ibn Sa'dan, from Abdullah ibn al-Qasim, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said:
The one whose right goes away without having any proof, would not be recompensed.
ai.seo_question: What is the legal consequence of losing a right without providing proof in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In Shia jurisprudence, this hadith from Al-Kafi underscores the necessity of 'bayyinah' (clear evidence) for establishing rights, reflecting the principle that uncertainty (gharar) invalidates the claim. It serves as a foundational text for legal proceedings, emphasizing that the burden of proof lies with the claimant, and without it, the status quo prevails. This principle is crucial in both financial transactions and inheritance cases within the Ja'fari school of thought.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Abu Abdullah, from Muhammad Bin Ali, from Musa Bin Sa’dan, from Abdullah Bin Al Qasim, from Abdullah Bin Sinan, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘The one whose right goes away upon without having any proof, would not be Recompensed’.
en.sarwar: 3. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn abu ‘Abd Allah from Muhammad ibn Ali from Musa ibn Sa‘dan from ‘Abd Allah ibn al-Qasim from ‘Abd Allah ibn Sinan who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘

One who loses his right just because of not having witnesses, does not receive any reward.’” Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Musa ibn Sa‘dan from ‘Abd Allah ibn Sinan abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, a similar Hadith.
